chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who died and bequeathed a Hajj. Is it permissible that Hajj be performed on his behalf from other than the city in which he died? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is below the Miqat, so there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمِيقَاتِ: The Miqat, the ritual boundary for entering Ihram

ai.seo_question: Can the Hajj of a deceased person be performed from a city other than where they died?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the geographical flexibility in performing the Hajj of a deceased person, a key issue in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of Ihram entry points. Imam al-Rida (AS) permits performing Hajj from any location south of the Miqat, emphasizing that the ritual boundary, not the place of death, determines the validity of the departure. This ruling facilitates the execution of bequeathed Hajj for those who die far from their home regions, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams.
